fema_nri.note: annualized_frequency = NRI <HAZ>_AFREQ (events/yr); eal_building_usd = <HAZ>_EALB (expected annual loss to ALL building value in the county, all occupancies); rating = <HAZ>_RISKR. Riverine flooding uses the IFLD prefix. building_value_usd = BUILDVALUE; eal_building_total_usd = EAL_VALB. v1.20 vs v1.19 for McLennan: hail EAL rose from $53K to $1.13M/yr (rating Relatively Low -> Relatively Moderate); winter-weather and heat-wave frequencies were redefined (0.93 -> 3.11 and 0.81 -> 16.9); building exposure rose from $50.1B to $56.2B. Hail EAL in McLennan ($1.1M) is far below Travis ($23.9M, v1.19) or Bexar ($28.5M, v1.19) despite similar or higher hail frequency: NRI's loss ratios reflect county loss history and exposure, so the hail rating understates physical hail exposure relative to Bell ($8.9M hail EAL on similar exposure). Tornado ($5.3M) is the largest roof-relevant EAL in McLennan.

Long, hot summers (NCEI: 58 Heat/Excessive Heat events 1996-2025; NRI heat wave Relatively Moderate in v1.20) accelerate membrane and coating aging, but NRI assigns ~$0 building loss and no source quantified a Waco roof-life penalty. code_triggers.text: Adoption: search excerpts of the City of Waco Code of Ordinances (Municode, Ch. 6 Buildings) show an ordinance adopting 'various 2024 International Codes relating to the construction, renovation, use and maintenance of buildings' plus the NEC as adopted by TDLR. The exact list (IBC/IEBC/IECC 2024?), effective date and local amendments were NOT verified: waco-texas.com and municode were blocked. Texas has no statewide commercial building code for most private buildings, so city adoption governs; unincorporated McLennan County has limited building-code enforcement (not verified). Model-code text (2024 IEBC, opened): (1) Sec. 705.3 - a roof RECOVER is not permitted where the existing roof is water-soaked or deteriorated so it is not an adequate base, where the covering is slate/clay/cement/asbestos-cement tile, or where the roof already has two or more applications of any covering; so neglect that lets water into insulation forces full tear-off. (2) Sec. 705.3.1 - new protective coatings over existing coatings, metal panels, BUR, SPF, mod bit and single-ply are permitted without tear-off (code basis for restoration). (3) Sec. 705.2 - roof replacement means removal of all layers down to the deck. (4) Sec. 705.1 - reroof of low-slope roofs is exempt from the 1/4:12 minimum slope and from adding secondary drains if positive drainage exists. (5) Sec. 706.2 - structural upgrade if dead load rises >5%, except a second roof layer <=3 psf over a single existing layer. (6) Sec. 708.1 - Level 1 alterations (incl. reroofing) must meet IECC requirements 'as they relate to new construction'. Energy: 2021 IECC C503.3.1 (search excerpt) requires roof replacement with insulation entirely above deck to meet the new-construction R-value; Climate Zone 2 = R-25ci (search excerpt, Carlisle/Versico SpecTopics); 2024 IECC value for CZ 2 not verified. No local percentage-of-damage rule forcing full replacement was found.
